cases.name: a * after a first ] repeats the empty class
cases.why: The reference reads `[]*]` as the class that matches nothing, any number of times, and then `]`. So `a[]*]` matches `a]`.

cases.name: a * after a first ] still needs the ]
cases.why: `a[]*]` does not match `a`.

cases.name: a ? after a first ] makes the empty class optional
cases.why: `src/[]?]` matches `src/]`.

cases.name: a count of zero after a first ] removes the empty class
cases.why: `a[]{0}]x` matches `a]x`.

cases.name: a | after a first ] splits the whole glob
cases.why: The second alternative is not held to the start of the path, so `ab[]|c]` matches every path that ends in `c]`.

cases.name: a | after a first ] does not match another ending
cases.why: The path must still end in `c]`.

cases.name: the part before a first ] with a | matches no path alone
cases.why: The first alternative holds the class that matches nothing.

cases.name: a glob after a first ] with a | is held to its directory
cases.why: `**` after the alternative matches as in any glob.

cases.name: a letter after a first ] is compared with case
cases.why: The claims dialect is case-sensitive in a class too.

cases.name: a . after a first ] matches one character
cases.why: The `.` is the dot of a regular expression.

cases.name: a ^ after a first ] holds the alternative to the start
cases.why: `[]|^b]` matches `b]`.

cases.name: a ^ after a first ] does not match after the start
cases.why: `[]|^b]` does not match `ab]`.

cases.name: a $ after a first ] matches no path before the ]
cases.why: The `]` of the class follows the `$`, so the alternative never matches.

cases.name: a count after a first ] needs its least number
cases.why: `a{2,3}` needs two `a`.

cases.name: a count after a first ] matches within its bounds
cases.why: `a{2,3}` matches two `a`.

cases.name: a { that starts no count is a character
cases.why: `{,2}` has no least number, so the reference reads its characters as they are.

cases.name: a group after a first ] can span two classes
cases.why: The `(` of the first class is closed by the `)` of the second.

cases.name: a group with a name after a first ] is a group
cases.why: `(?<n>a)+` matches one `a` or more.

cases.name: a lookbehind after a first ] matches after its text
cases.why: `(?<=b)]` matches a `]` that follows `b`.

cases.name: a lookbehind after a first ] does not match after other text
cases.why: `(?<=b)]` does not match a `]` that follows `a`.

cases.name: a negative lookbehind after a first ] matches after other text
cases.why: `(?<!b)c` matches a `c` that does not follow `b`.

cases.name: a negative lookbehind after a first ] does not match after its text
cases.why: `(?<!b)c` does not match a `c` that follows `b`.

cases.name: a lookahead after a first ] matches before its text
cases.why: `(?=c)c` matches `c`.

cases.name: a negative lookahead after a first ] does not match before its text
cases.why: `(?!c).` does not match `c`.

cases.name: a negative lookahead after a first ] matches before other text
cases.why: `(?!c).` matches `d`.

cases.name: a \ after a first ] is a separator
cases.why: A `\` is `/` before the glob is read, so `\d` is `/d` and not a digit.

cases.name: two globs overlap when one matches the literal prefix of the other
cases.why: The literal prefix of `zc]*` is `zc]`, which `ab[]|c]` matches. Neither literal prefix starts the other.

cases.name: two globs do not overlap when neither matches the prefix of the other
cases.why: The literal prefix of `zd]*` is `zd]`, which `ab[]|c]` does not match.

informational.error: Invalid regular expression: /^[z-a]$/: Range out of order in character class

cases.name: a range that is out of order throws against a path
cases.why: The reference throws when it reads the glob. The seventh open question of the README gives the rule.

informational.error: Invalid regular expression: /^[z-a]$/: Range out of order in character class

cases.name: a range that is out of order throws against the same glob
cases.why: The reference reads a glob before it compares two globs. The seventh open question of the README gives the rule.

informational.error: Invalid regular expression: /^[z-a][^/]*$/: Range out of order in character class

cases.name: a range that is out of order throws against another glob
cases.why: The reference reads the first glob before it compares the literal prefixes. The seventh open question of the README gives the rule.

cases.name: a glob that matches the empty prefix of a glob that throws overlaps it
cases.why: The reference reads the first glob, finds that it matches the literal prefix of the second, and never reads the second. With the two in the other order it throws.

cases.name: a group that is not closed throws
cases.why: `[](]` is the regular expression `[](]`. The seventh open question of the README gives the rule.

informational.error: Invalid regular expression: /^[]|*]$/: Nothing to repeat

cases.name: a * with nothing to repeat throws
cases.why: In `[]|*]` no term is before the `*`. The seventh open question of the README gives the rule.

informational.error: Invalid regular expression: /^[]**]$/: Nothing to repeat

cases.name: a ** after a first ] throws
cases.why: The second `*` has nothing to repeat. The seventh open question of the README gives the rule.

informational.error: Invalid regular expression: /^[]|a{3,2}]$/: numbers out of order in {} quantifier

cases.name: a count with its bounds out of order throws
cases.why: `a{3,2}` has a least number above its greatest. The seventh open question of the README gives the rule.

informational.error: Invalid regular expression: /^[]|(?<n>a)(?<n>b)]$/: Duplicate capture group name

cases.name: two groups with the same name throw
cases.why: A name can be used once. The seventh open question of the README gives the rule.

description: Whether two patterns overlap when one holds a class whose first character is `]`, or a range that is out of order. The reference reads such a class as regular expression syntax, or throws.
